messages:
Sarah (Acme): Hey team — running into a weird SSE problem from a Safari 16/17 webview. On an authenticated stream (we use a cookie for session), the stream sends a few events (sometimes partial lines), then stops emitting for ~20s and the client reconnects. When it reconnects sometimes we see a 401 from the CDN edge then back to 200, sometimes a 304. Repro steps below. Any ideas?

Sarah (Acme): Repro (minimal):
1) Open Safari (mac or iOS webview)
2) window.eventSource = new EventSource("https://api.example.com/v1/stream?room=123", { withCredentials: true });
3) server emits events every 2s; after ~10-30s client shows no 'message' events, then EventSource.readyState goes to 0 -> reconnect, sometimes 401 first.

Sarah (Acme): Network notes from devtools HAR: a few 200s with Transfer-Encoding: chunked, then a 304 with CF-Cache-Status: HIT, then a 200 with Set-Cookie (same session), then socket closes. Also sometimes Content-Encoding: gzip present.

Micah (Support): thanks — can you paste the raw response headers for the SSE 200 and the 304? also do you have HAR? if not, a quick curl test that mimics the cookie would help.

Sarah (Acme): HAR attached (link). Raw headers for a 200 chunk:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: public, max-age=0
CF-Cache-Status: PASS
Content-Encoding: gzip
Set-Cookie: session=abc; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Path=/
Vary: Cookie
```
And later the 304: 
```
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
CF-Cache-Status: HIT
Age: 123
Vary: Cookie
```

Micah (Support): hm — cookie+CDN caching + gzip + Safari = several red flags. EventSource in browsers can't set custom headers, so people either rely on cookies or put token in query param. Safari has known buffering behaviour when proxies compress or buffer chunks.

Jonas (SRE): +1 — CDNs sometimes convert chunked streaming into cached objects (buffer until a threshold) or serve 304s based on Vary. If the CDN is treating the stream response as cacheable and then later returns a cached 304, the browser will try to reattach to the existing connection and Safari's EventSource implementation can mishandle that sequence and drop events. Also compression at the edge will cause small chunks to be buffered until buffer full -> Safari sees big gaps.

Eva (Eng Runtime): quick checklist we usually ask for:
- Is Content-Type exactly text/event-stream (no extra tokens)?
- Are we sending SSE comment heartbeats (':\n\n' or ': keepalive\n\n') at least every 15s?
- Is Transfer-Encoding: chunked and the origin calling flush on each event?
- Is there any edge setting that enables gzip/deflate for streaming responses? some CDNs force gzip and that will buffer.

Sarah (Acme): Content-Type is text/event-stream; we do emit a JSON event every ~2s. We do not have heartbeats. The CDN is CloudFront in front of our origin and yes it has compression enabled for that route.

Eva (Eng Runtime): ok probable cause: CDN is compressing & caching parts of the stream and the cookie + Vary headers are creating cache behavior (304s). Safari buffers/chunks + reconnect semantics -> partial frames then reconnect. Workarounds:
- Set Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform, private on the SSE response so CDN does not compress or cache.
- Add Vary: Authorization (if you switch to tokens) or avoid Vary: Cookie on streaming paths.
- Add a frequent SSE comment heartbeat, flush after each write. Example Node/Express snippet: 
```js
res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/event-stream');
res.setHeader('Cache-Control','no-cache, no-transform, private');
res.setHeader('Connection','keep-alive');
// important for cross-site cookie auth + SSE
res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Credentials','true');
res.flushHeaders();

const heartbeat = setInterval(() => {
  // colon-prefixed comment is ignored by client but forces flush
  res.write(':\\n\\n');
}, 15000);

// emit an event
res.write('event: message\\n');
res.write('data: ' + JSON.stringify({ hello: 'world' }) + '\\n\\n');
res.flush && res.flush(); // if using compression middleware flush function

// on close
req.on('close', () => { clearInterval(heartbeat); });
```
Jonas (SRE): also add Surrogate-Control: no-store if you have intermediary caches (CF) or configure the CDN route to disable caching + disable compression on the origin/route. On CloudFront set Content-Encoding passthrough and turn off behavior that gzips responses.

Micah (Support): small UX note: EventSource can't attach Authorization header, so if you need header auth you must proxy the stream through a short-lived endpoint that takes a header and then opens the SSE to the client (or switch to token in query param). Cookies + SameSite can be fragile in embedded webviews — confirm SameSite=None; Secure required for cross-site.

Sarah (Acme): OK — quick test: turned off CloudFront compression and added Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform to SSE route. Still seeing occasional stalls but much reduced. When it does stall, console shows no messages for ~22s then reconnects. Do you think that's due to missing heartbeats?

Eva (Eng Runtime): yes. Safari can coalesce small writes if no explicit flush/heartbeat. Add the comment heartbeat and ensure you flush after each event. If using a language runtime that buffers (e.g., Go's ResponseWriter with gzip middleware), the middleware may re-buffer. If you can't disable gzip globally, ensure the SSE route bypasses compression middleware.

Jonas (SRE): another thing — if the origin returns a 304 on HEAD/conditional GET semantics, the browser may revalidate and then close/reopen sockets. For SSE we should never return 304s; set Cache-Control: no-cache and remove ETag/Vary for stream endpoints so conditional response flow is bypassed.

Sarah (Acme): Great we removed ETag and Vary: Cookie for the stream route and added heartbeats + no-transform. Seems stable in my local Safari and iOS webview tests. One remaining weirdness: when the iOS webview backgrounded and resumed, sometimes the stream reconnects but the first few events are missing (partial). That feels like state loss at our side.

Micah (Support): when webview backgrounding happens, the TCP connection can be paused by the OS. Make sure your server doesn't treat a connection as stale and drop immediately on short pauses; increase idle threshold on origin keep-alive for mobile clients. Also check that your client logic for handling 'retry' doesn't inadvertently drop last event-id. If you rely on Last-Event-ID, ensure the server honours it to resume from an event boundary.

Eva (Eng Runtime): follow-up items for eng runtime if we escalate:
- Confirm our public docs show recommended SSE headers (no-transform, no-cache, Connection keep-alive)
- Provide an example CloudFront behavior for streaming routes (disable cache + compression)
- Consider an SDK helper that exchanges a bearer token over XHR then returns a short-lived query token for SSE (so clients don't rely on cookies).

Micah (Support): Sarah — can you confirm the timeline after the changes? if it's stable we'll close; if you still see partial frames please attach a HAR and we can escalate to eng-runtime.

Sarah (Acme): Thanks all — after the changes (disable compression, add heartbeats, no-transform + remove ETag/Vary) things are stable across Safari desktop and iOS webview for 24h test. I'll reopen if we see regressions. Really appreciate the fast triage 🙏

deploy-bot: "Reminder: streaming-route cache and compression flags were updated in CDN staging at 2026-11-05T03:12Z"

Micah (Support): Marking as resolved for now. If it recurs we'll reopen and attach HAR + logs. :thumbsup:
